name: Mysuru
method: automated: web search + Claude compile + page verification (scripts/research_stunting_districts.py)
headline: Street children face severe undernutrition; Mysuru reports declining malnutrition through targeted interventions
summary: Mysuru district recorded 36.8% stunting among street children and 142 underweight children in 2025-26, down from 692 in 2023-24—a 79% reduction. In 2021, 9,515 children suffered malnutrition, with 135 cases of Severe Acute Malnutrition, and 1,500 malnourished children in H.D. Kote taluk alone. Despite progress, anaemia remains prevalent. CFTRI launched a Nutrition Intervention Programme in 2025 providing scientifically developed food kits to 500 Anganwadi children. District officials in 2021 set a goal to eliminate malnutrition by 2023 through awareness and nutritious food provision.

reasons.detail: Among street children in Mysuru, 76.5% were underweight and 36.8% stunted, indicating severe chronic undernutrition in this marginalized group.
52.5% of street children and high rates among pregnant women indicate widespread iron deficiency affecting child growth outcomes.
H.D. Kote taluk, predominantly tribal with forests and hamlets, had 1,500 of the district's 9,515 malnourished children in 2021.
In 2025, despite 91 identified malnourished children, beds at Cheluvamba Hospital's exclusive ward remained empty with insufficient dietary ingredients.
CFTRI's 2025 intervention provides energy-protein burfi, spirulina chikki, and supplements to 500 Anganwadi children with micronutrient testing.

modelFactorWhy.factor: Mothers who took iron-folic acid for 180+ days in pregnancy
modelFactorWhy.why: Research confirms anaemia prevalence among pregnant women in rural Mysuru, and 52.5% anaemia among street children indicates maternal iron deficiency impacts. However, no district data quantifies IFA compliance rates locally.
modelFactorWhy.mechanism: Maternal iron-folic acid intake reduces anaemia risk in children, lowering stunting by improving fetal development and birth weight.

proof.claim: 52.5% of street children in Mysuru had anaemia, often linked to maternal nutrition
Anaemia screening studies conducted among pregnant women in rural Mysuru areas

modelFactorWhy.why: No district-specific data found on preschool enrollment rates or school-going status among 3-6 year olds in Mysuru. The focus is on Anganwadi attendance rather than formal schooling for this age group.
modelFactorWhy.mechanism: Preschool attendance enables nutritional supplementation, early health screening, and developmental monitoring that prevent stunting.

modelFactorWhy.factor: Household members covered by health insurance
modelFactorWhy.why: No pages discuss health insurance coverage rates in Mysuru households. References to health services focus on government programmes, not insurance penetration or its effect on child nutrition outcomes.
modelFactorWhy.mechanism: Health insurance coverage improves healthcare access for maternal and child services, enabling timely treatment of illnesses that contribute to stunting.

gaps: No local data on IFA compliance rates, preschool enrollment, health insurance coverage, or specific stunting prevalence beyond street children.
